events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body: This is a driver-cancelled no-show fee dispute, so it enters through NS-0, which routes a cancelled_by = driver case where the driver claims rider no-show into NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. The trace settles the three NS-1 elements: the driver did tap "I'm Here" at 22:37:10 [F5], but at that moment he was 1000 m from the pickup point and his closest approach overall was 868 m, so NS-1 (ii) fails [F5][F1][NS-1]; and he spent 0 s inside the 200 m radius after the tap, so NS-1 (iii) also fails [F5][NS-1]. The platform never recorded him at the pickup at all (driver_arrived_at null) and his 5 min 5 s stationary period ran 993 m away [F4][F2][NS-1]. claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 868 m at 22:36:25 and GPS records that he never came within 200 m of the pickup point.
When the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:10 he was 1000 m away from the pickup point, and he spent 0 seconds inside the 200 m pickup radius afterwards, so NS-1 condition (ii) fails.

The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), and he was stationary 22:36:45–22:41:50 about 993 m away, so his waiting time was not served at the pickup point as NS-1 (iii) requires.
Because a NS-1 condition fails, the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full.

The driver's written claim that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the system records (he tapped 1000 m away and waited 993 m away), so it cannot support the fee.
The rider's own message at 22:38 saying she was at the pickup point and saw no car matches the GPS record that no car was within 200 m, so the no-show allegation against her is unsupported.
The driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS shows he was not at the pickup point, which is the abuse-of-cancellation/waiting-button situation that warrants an account flag in addition to the refund.

weaknesses: The driver did wait stationary for 5 min 5 s (F2) and cancelled 8 min 50 s after acceptance (F3), so the timing of the wait looks superficially like a genuine pickup attempt; we rely on the fact that the wait occurred ~993 m away (F2, F4).

The chat (F8) shows the driver claiming he was already at the pickup, and the driver's statement (F12) repeats that he waited over 3 minutes; the judge must prefer the system records per the record-priority rule.
Light rain (F15) could be argued as a reason for stopping short of the pickup, though no traffic incident or speed-band record supports any obstruction on the route (F13, F14).
The rider's 90-day history shows 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F16), a neutral point that the other side may cite, though profile facts cannot decide the case.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here", but the GPS record shows he was 1000 m from the pickup point when he tapped it at 22:37:10, so the first NS-1 requirement (arrival at the pickup point) is not met on the system record.
The driver never entered the pickup area at all: his closest approach was 868 m at 22:36:25 and he spent 0 seconds within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii) cannot be satisfied.
The driver's 5 min 5 s stationary period from 22:36:45 to 22:41:50 was 993 m from the pickup point, so the time he waited was not waiting at the pickup location as NS-1 (iii) requires.

The driver's own written statement ("I pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup") and his in-app message "I'm here already" are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (never within 200 m, driver_arrived_at null) and under the system-records-priority rule they cannot establish arrival.
Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged to the rider must be refunded in full under NS-2.

The rider's account of waiting at the pickup point is corroborated by her contemporaneous 22:38 message asking where the driver was, sent while the driver was stationary 993 m away — there is no evidence of rider no-show.

No external cause excuses the non-arrival: no traffic incidents and no speed-band records exist for the route in the trip window, and the only environmental factor was light rain (1.8 mm), which does not explain a 993 m stop-off.

The driver had two no-show disputes upheld in the last 90 days, so the same failure mode is repeated and flag_account is appropriate alongside the refund, on the basis of the profile record only as an add-on action.
The $6.61 fee is the only amount disputed and no surge applies (1.0×), so the refund amount is exactly the $6.61 recorded as charged.
The chat record is complete (3 messages, all timestamped) and contains no threat, intimidation or harassment, so no SAFE-1 escalation is triggered; the case is decided on the no-show clauses.

weaknesses: The driver did tap "I'm Here" and did wait over 3 minutes, which superficially matches NS-1 wording for (i) and the duration in (iii); the rider side will lean on the tap itself (F5) and the driver's message "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" (F10) as if arrival were established.

The driver has 1152 trips in 90 days and a 4.84 rating from 5.7 years on the platform (F17), which the rider will use to argue this was an isolated mis-click rather than a pattern — cutting against a flag_account request, even though the profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days.

Light rain (F15) gives the rider no help, but it equally gives the driver no excuse; the driver might try to argue weather caused the 993 m stop-off, and the traffic record is empty (F13, F14), so no traffic defence exists either.
The GPS record is dense and unambiguous (F1, F2, F5) and there is no missing-record gap to argue about, so there is no G12 route to 'undetermined' for the driver.

If the driver were instead treated as having cancelled for a non-no-show reason, NS-3 would also produce a full refund and additionally expose the driver's cancellation-rate account action — the weaker position for the client.

Agreed on the rider's brief too: the driver's own profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 d (F17), which supports flag_account only as an add-on to the refund under NS-2, never as the basis of the finding.
Agreed — the disputed amount is the $6.61 cancellation fee with no surge (F6, F7), so the refund figure is $6.61.

Agreed — the chat record is complete with 3 timestamped messages (F11) and nothing in F8–F10 reads as a threat, intimidation or harassment, so no SAFE-1 escalation is triggered and the case is decided on the no-show clauses.

Conceded as to the system record: GPS shows the closest approach was 868 m at 22:36:25 and the driver never came within 200 m (F1), so NS-1 (ii) fails on that record — but the record also shows he did stop and wait 5 min 5 s at that spot (F2), which is why the fee was charged in good faith rather than invented.

Conceded: the tap at 22:37:10 was made 1000 m from the pickup point with 0 s inside 200 m afterwards (F5), so NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied for this case; this is the decisive point and my client does not contest it.

Conceded on the facts (F4, F2), with one qualification that does not change the outcome: the 5 min 5 s stationary period and the absence of any traffic incident or speed-band record in the window (F13, F14) show the driver's own conduct, not an external obstruction, produced the standstill 993 m short.
Agreed, and consistent with my claim D5: with NS-1 (i)-(iii) unmet the $6.61 is not chargeable and NS-2 requires a full refund of the fee recorded at F6 (F3, F6).

No objection — I already request this in D8: the tap at 1000 m from the pickup (F5) while GPS shows non-arrival is the abuse-of-the-cancellation-button situation, and the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) support flag_account alongside the refund; profile facts carry the add-on action only, and the refund stands on NS-2 independently.
